oracle.efficient: answer(): f(s)=number of adjacent ".." pairs (each replacement shortens a period run by one, lowering the pair count by exactly one; operation is forced, so the minimum equals that count); updated in O(1) per query by removing/adding the pairs (x-1,x),(x,x+1).
independent: literal_answers(): rebuilds the string after each query and literally replaces the first ".." with "." until none remain, counting operations
run_answers(): periods minus maximal period runs, updated with a different run-merge/split formula
pairs_from_scratch() in tests: regex over the whole string at checkpoints (every query for small m, >=50 checkpoints per case incl. max size)
minimum_any_occurrence() in tests: BFS over replacing ANY ".." occurrence for all 2^n strings n<=8, confirming the minimum equals the forced first-occurrence count

problem.title: Replacement

wrongAnswer.57922619: genuine: n=1 prints one line only; IndexError at x=n

semantics: n,m 1..300000 (literal "300 000" in the public statement, no flattened exponent); line 2 is s of exactly n characters from a-z and "."; then exactly m lines "x c" with 1<=x<=n and c one of a-z or ".". Each replacement turns the first ".." into ".", shortening one period run by one and lowering the number of adjacent ".." pairs by exactly one, so f(s) is that pair count. The unique output is m integers, one per line, each in 0..n-1. answer() updates the pair count locally around x; independently checked by literal first-occurrence replacement simulation, exhaustive single assignments, and a periods-minus-runs count.
